newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 8.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 8.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
MARKETING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - Shares in German television network ProSieben Media AG jump 32 percent as they traded for the first time, outstripping even major DAX companies with a traded volume of 2.7 million shares. Yet the closing price of 95 marks ($54.22), up from an issue price of 72 marks, was lower than many traders had hoped. (Reuter)

BONN - Business leaders and politicians gather from all over the world and urge the European Union to take a soft-line toward cyberspace laws. In meetings between more than 40 government ministers and some 80 business leaders at the EU's Global Information Network conference, participants call for more private sector efforts to establish fair play on the Internet. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Greeting the success of Pro Sieben Media AG's bourse debut, board member Michael Woelfle says he expects the company's television channels to keep expanding in the German advertising market. Woelfle says the group's largest station, Pro Sieben, has long-term growth potential of 20 percent from advertising and the company's number two station, Kabel 1, will likely develop its ad base at an even greater rate. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Media group WAZ of Essen plans a complete takeover of the largest Bulgarian newspaper publisher 168 Tschassa (168 Hours). WAZ acquired 70 percent of the company earlier this year. (Handelsblatt)

FRANKFURT - ProSieben Media AG chairman Georg Kofler points to the success of its TV advertising campaign as paving the way to a high-profile public listing. Kofler says the TV ad campaign for its bourse launch had been second in size in German history only to Deutsche Telekom's share debut promotion last fall and credits it with giving Monday's start marquee value. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The chairman of ProSieben Media AG says there was "no chance" of shareholders manipulating TV ratings of stations owned by the company. Kofler says that when the GfK media research group collects viewer data, it excludes households which leave their set tuned to ProSieben stations for the entire night. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Directly after Canal Plus agreed to take over the 45 percent share in Italian pay TV company Telepiu SpA owned by media mogul Leo Kirch, a bank consortium extended a medium-term credit of 700 million marks for the company. (Handelsblatt)
BERLIN - "Seinfeld", the most popular sitcom in America, dies on German television, where viewers prefer vintage episodes of "Hogan's Heroes".
"The humor is simply too American," says Nickolas Paalzow, head of programming at Kabel 1. " 'Seinfeld' takes place in a world most Germans cannot relate to." (Variety)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MUNICH - Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) strongly denies a press report it is considering selling the small car unit of its Rover Group to Chrysler Corp. The Times newspaper reports Chrysler is trying to buy Rover's small car division. A BMW spokesman calls the report "complete nonsense." (Reuter)

BONN - German officials say they have seized a cargo of beef from Belgium which they believed was British meat exported illegally in defiance of a worldwide export ban. The agriculture ministry in the northern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern says the meat was seized at the port of Mukran on the island of Ruegen at the weekend.
(Reuter)

COLOGNE - German insurers Gothaer Versicherungen and Berlin-Koelnischen Versicherungen say they have linked up to create a new firm called Parion. Wolfgang Peiner, the new group's chairman, says German insurers need to link up to improve their chances of survival. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - The designated head of the planned new German insurer ERGO Versicherungsgruppe says the group will want to expand in Europe through acquisitions. Reinsurance group Munich Re announces that ERGO, a holding company in which it will have a majority stake, will be created by the fusion of Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Charter airline Britannia Airways plans to compete with German airlines Condor and LTU in the German market. Britannia director Richard Manley says his company has formed a German unit, Britannia Airways GmbH, which will begin working with partner Frosch Touristik International in November. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Chief executive of Initiative Media in Hamburg, Ernstwilhelm Woehler, is the company's new chairman of the board. He replaces Hans Germeraad, who is moving to the board of HMS Carat Deutschland. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Lorenz Zehetbauer is new chief executive of publishing group Weltbild in Augsburg. He was previously financial director of Bayerischen Rundfunk. (Kress)
